# Key Secrecy Checklist: Maxitor Opens a History and Shows Any Version

**Purpose**: Test whether the requirements say, for every place a read key could surface, that it does not — URLs, logs, errors, the screen, storage, outbound links, rooms
**Created**: 2026-10-29
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) · [research.md](../research.md) · [contracts/maxitor-api.md](../contracts/maxitor-api.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Does the spec itself, not only research R1, say where the key sits in a history's address, so that FR-001's "carries its read key" is testable without reading the plan? [Traceability, Spec §FR-001, Research R1]
- [ ] CHK002 Are all the ways a key travels listed in one requirement — typed address, page address, Maxitor's API reads, the room's WebSocket, the room link, Recent, the copied link — each with where the key may and may not be? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010, §FR-011, Research R2]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the browser's own address bar covered? FR-010 lists the field, Recent and the room link, but `#key=` shows in full in the address bar of every history page, on a shared screen or in a screenshot. [Gap, Spec §FR-010, Data model "Page address"]
- [ ] CHK004 Is the browser's history (and history synced between devices) addressed as a place where the page address, key included, is kept? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK005 Do the requirements name every log Maxitor writes — its actions' log, uvicorn's access log, error tracebacks — rather than "no log Maxitor writes"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011, Research R3]
- [ ] CHK006 Is the stand's HTTPS front end (a log Maxitor does not write) covered by a requirement, or only by research R1's reasoning about fragments? [Traceability, Research R1]
- [ ] CHK007 Are error texts — the answers Maxitor gives the browser, and the reasons it shows on screen — required to carry no key and no whole address? Today the loader's errors quote the URL (`{url!r}`). [Gap, Spec §FR-008, Contract maxitor-api "Refusals"]
- [ ] CHK008 Is it required that the in-memory record of a history (its remembered key) never appears in a `repr`, an exception, a debug dump or a test's failure output? Today only the data model says so. [Traceability, Data model "HistoryEntry"]
- [ ] CHK009 Is telemetry or tracing (if Maxitor sends any) covered, as #288 covered it for the port? [Gap, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the store's key — the source string a version is held under — required to be keyless in the spec, not only in research R4? [Traceability, Research R4]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the room's WebSocket address required to carry the history without the key? Only the room contract says so. [Traceability, Contract room-protocol "Opening"]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK012 Does "shown as dots" say how many dots, whether the key's length shows, and whether the part of the address after the key (if any) stays readable? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK013 Is it clear that the room link is shown with dots but copied with the real key — and what a shared copy, pasted into a chat, then exposes? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-010, Assumptions "room link"]
- [ ] CHK014 Is "the eye reveals it" specified for how long: until clicked again (US2 scenario 3), or also until the field is left (contract ui.md)? [Conflict, Spec §US2, Contract ui "The address field"]
- [ ] CHK015 Is "a short hash of the address" fixed in length and algorithm, so that two log readers agree on what identifies a source? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011, Research R3]
- [ ] CHK016 Is "the key's name" in logs defined as the port's `reader`, and is what is logged for a public link stated? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011, Contract port]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK017 Do FR-009 (the same "not found"), the API contract (`404 {"detail": "not found"}`) and the room contract (a refused `version` answered with an `error` reason) agree that no answer tells a wrong key from a missing history or version? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009, Contracts maxitor-api, room-protocol]
- [ ] CHK018 Is keeping the whole address, key included, in Recent's browser storage (research R14) consistent with FR-010's intent, and is it written as an accepted risk in the spec's Assumptions? [Assumption, Research R14]
- [ ] CHK019 Are outbound links other than the message's — a Live service's address, the repository, a version on GitHub, if the screen links any — held to the same "no `Referer`, no Maxitor address" rule as FR-028a? [Consistency, Spec §FR-028a]

## Scenario and Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK020 Is it specified within what time a revoked or expired key stops opening versions Maxitor already holds, as a measurable criterion, not only as research R6's 30 seconds? [Measurability, Spec §FR-009, Research R6]
- [ ] CHK021 Is the port's per-client limit on wrong keys addressed? Every Maxitor reader reaches the port from Maxitor's one address, so one person's wrong keys could get every Maxitor user refused with `429`. [Gap, Dependency, #288 FR-012]
- [ ] CHK022 Is Maxitor's answer to the port's `429` specified? [Gap, Contract maxitor-api "Refusals"]
- [ ] CHK023 Is it specified what a room shows to a joiner whose link lost its key (the fragment stripped by a messenger): the room's pages and names before any diagram fails? [Gap, Research R9]
- [ ] CHK024 Is it specified which key the room's server uses after the key it remembered is revoked, while other participants still hold valid keys? [Edge Case, Gap, Research R7, R9]
- [ ] CHK025 Is it specified that a user can remove a history (and its key) from Recent, and that leaving a room or closing the tab does not leave the key anywhere but Recent? [Gap, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK026 Are the page's title, tooltips and notices (for example "History … opened") required to name a history without its address? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK027 Is a key pasted with surrounding spaces, or a second `#` in the address, covered so the stored key and the masked one are the same string? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK028 Does SC-004 say what is searched for the key — Maxitor's log file, its standard output, uvicorn's access log, error bodies, the stand's front-end log — so it can be measured, not judged? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK029 Is there a success criterion that the key never reaches any server other than the port, covering Maxitor's request lines and the `Referer` of outbound links? [Gap, Spec §Success Criteria]
